native_decision.hypothesis: An opt-in, explicitly typed source-location projection can add precise function and finding spans while preserving canonical evidence, IDs, scores, line fields, and legacy exports.
native_decision.reason: The receiving analyzer retains decoded source and AST line ranges but emits only line endpoints for functions, findings, and SARIF regions. The donor demonstrates the relevant mechanism: project each endpoint of a byte span independently into a declared external coordinate system, including variable-width UTF-16 character accounting. This supports an additive receiving design without asserting a runtime defect.
native_decision.adaptation: Add an opt-in receiving-specific location projection derived from admitted source bytes, the detected decoding, and AST endpoint metadata. Keep canonical line fields and finding IDs unchanged. Represent coordinate kind and end convention explicitly; preserve AST UTF-8 byte-column evidence where available, project start and exclusive end independently to the selected character unit, and retain original-file byte offsets only when the decoded-to-original mapping is determinable. Mark unavailable endpoints unknown rather than fabricating them. Populate opt-in SARIF columns only after converting to SARIF's declared coordinate convention; default bundles and SARIF remain byte-for-byte behaviorally unchanged.
native_decision.maintenance: Centralize endpoint projection and coordinate metadata so function records, findings, and opt-in exporters share one conversion contract. Document one-based lines, the chosen column base/unit, exclusive-end semantics, handling of encoding markers and newline forms, and explicit unknown values. Keep the feature disabled by default and avoid new parsing, execution, rendering, authority, scoring, or health semantics.
native_decision.acceptance: Original receiving-only design cases establish that: (1) without the option, analysis and SARIF retain their existing shapes and values; (2) enabling projection does not change canonical IDs, line/end_line, scores, evidence, ordering, coverage, or policy/resource outcomes; (3) ASCII, non-ASCII BMP, supplementary Unicode, CRLF, and multiline functions/findings produce independently projected start and exclusive-end coordinates in the declared unit; (4) AST UTF-8 byte columns are not mislabeled as character columns; (5) original-file byte offsets are retained when mapping is available and otherwise are explicitly unknown; (6) missing AST endpoints, including synthetic whole-file findings, do not receive invented columns; and (7) opt-in SARIF emits startColumn/endColumn only after correct conversion while legacy SARIF remains unchanged.
native_decision.novelty: Within the explicit selected/default/confirmed-pending scope, evaluate and sarif contain no character-span projection: selected and several confirmed pending heads have identical declarations, older heads lack the subsystem, and the only supplied differing pending declaration changes history-proof/engine behavior rather than locations. Issue 76 is merely open and does not establish an implementation. Unrelated repository history remains unknown but is not needed for this scoped design finding.
native_decision.source_behavior: The donor converts a byte-span range by converting its start and end byte indices separately into LSP positions. Its reverse conversion scans Unicode scalar values and advances the external character offset by each scalar's UTF-16 width, accepting the position after the final character and rejecting an out-of-range position.

native_decision.hypothesis: An opt-in, explicitly typed projection from retained Python AST byte offsets to exporter-specific character coordinates would let consumers locate analyzed functions and findings precisely without altering canonical evidence or legacy output.
native_decision.reason: The receiving evaluator currently emits only one-based line/end_line values for functions and findings, and SARIF exports only startLine/endLine. The donor demonstrates the relevant mechanism: preserve byte-based source evidence and convert each half-open endpoint at an output boundary using an explicitly defined character unit. Adapting that mechanism would improve editor and SARIF precision while preserving IDs, scores, existing line fields, and default bundles.
native_decision.adaptation: Add an opt-in location projection for AST-backed functions and findings. Retain available original zero-based UTF-8 byte columns and expose a separately typed projected span whose lines remain one-based and whose columns have a declared unit and half-open end convention. Compute projections from the already decoded source, treating CRLF consistently and returning unknown endpoints rather than fabricated columns when no AST endpoint exists. Keep legacy analysis and SARIF unchanged by default; when SARIF columns are requested, convert the internal coordinate kind to SARIF's required one-based column representation rather than relabeling incompatible units.
native_decision.maintenance: Centralize byte-to-character conversion and coordinate metadata instead of duplicating exporter arithmetic. Keep projection opt-in and dependency-light, bound conversion work to admitted source and existing resource limits, preserve byte evidence for diagnostics, and require each future exporter to declare or convert its coordinate kind explicitly.
native_decision.acceptance: Original receiving-specific cases establish that: (1) default analysis and SARIF are byte-for-byte unchanged and canonical finding IDs, scores, line/end_line values, legacy bundles, safety guards, and policy results remain unchanged; (2) opted-in ASCII function and finding spans report the expected one-based lines and declared character columns with a half-open end; (3) non-ASCII text before and within a multiline node is projected from retained UTF-8 byte offsets without splitting a code point; (4) CRLF input maps endpoints to the correct logical lines and excludes line terminators consistently; (5) multiline definitions have independently projected start and end endpoints; (6) findings without usable AST endpoints retain their existing line range and report unknown byte/character endpoints; (7) opted-in SARIF emits valid one-based startColumn/endColumn values after an explicit conversion from the internal coordinate kind; and (8) repeated projection is deterministic and remains subject to existing admission and resource limits.
native_decision.novelty: Within the declared complete implementation scope, selected evaluate records only line/end_line for functions and findings, while selected sarif emits only startLine/endLine. The selected declarations are identical across the confirmed PR-81, PR-75, PR-88, PR-89, and PR-90 heads; older default and pending heads lack these files, and the differing PR-95 declarations concern history-proof accounting and engine version selection rather than source-character spans. Thus no equivalent implementation is present in the supplied selected/default/confirmed-pending scope; unrelated global history remains unknown but is not needed for this scoped conclusion.
